title: Calendula and chamomile face balm
subtitle: An anhydrous balm for dry and sensitive skin
excerpt: A simple anhydrous face balm of calendula-infused oil, beeswax, and dried chamomile, for dry and sensitive skin. Melts on contact with warmth and absorbs slowly. Makes one 30 ml tin; keeps a year.
sourceNotes: Calendula officinalis in cosmetic balms: EMA HMPC monograph on Calendula officinalis (2008, ema.europa.eu). Chamomile in cosmetics: EMA HMPC monograph on Matricaria chamomilla (2015). Beeswax-to-oil ratios for face balm: standard cosmetic formulation reference (20-30% beeswax for a soft, skin-spreadable balm).

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to two 30 ml tins without any adjustment. Keep the beeswax percentage the same.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make one tin at a time; keeps a year, so there is no need to batch in large quantities.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed tin in a cool, dark cupboard. The beeswax hardens slightly in cold weather; warm the tin briefly in your palms before use. Discard if the surface develops white spots or the balm smells sharp or rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation that contains no water. Anhydrous balms keep for a year or more without a preservative because water-loving microbes have nothing to grow on. They are slower to absorb than water-containing creams but more concentrated.

content.text: face balm made with calendula-infused oil and beeswax, for dry and sensitive skin. Calendula-infused sunflower or olive oil is gentle on reactive skin; chamomile flowers in the blend add a faint herb note. The balm melts on contact with skin warmth and absorbs slowly as the oils work in. Apply a thin layer over dry patches at night or over a moisturiser in cold weather.
Patch test on the inside of the forearm before use. Leave for 24 hours.

items.prepNote: calendula in sunflower or olive oil; 73% of formula
cosmetic grade; 20% of formula; gives the firm-but-spreadable consistency
7% of formula; gentle and optional; omit for a truly unscented version

content.text: Combine the beeswax and the calendula-infused oil in a heatproof glass bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water. Stir gently until the beeswax is fully melted. Remove from the heat.
Allow the mixture to cool to 55°C. Stir in the lavender essential oil if using. Pour immediately into the tin. The mixture sets quickly once off the heat.
Leave the tin on a flat surface for two hours. Do not move it while the surface sets or the top will wrinkle. Once firm, press on the lid.
Apply a small amount to the inside of the forearm. Leave for 24 hours before using on the face. Discontinue if any redness, itching, or irritation develops.
Keeps one year in a sealed tin in a cool, dark cupboard. Discard if the balm smells rancid or the surface develops white bloom.
